headline: The ledger grew from 20 entries to 68: every one of the 20 seed entries is byte-identical to what was on disk before this pass, and 48 new entries were added across six families named in G055's brief. Five of the 48 cite a real receipt already in this repo as measured evidence (ACCELERATOR_DEVICE_RESIDENT, ACCELERATOR_GRAPH_SUBMISSION, ACCELERATOR_JIT_COMPILE, ACCELERATOR_EXPERT_BATCH, ACCELERATOR_REGISTER_BLOCKING); the other 43 are honestly UNMEASURED with a specific reason each, not a generic placeholder.

hard_rules_upheld.no_unqualified_cuda_parity_phrase: grepped the regenerated ledger and ccl.py for the literal phrase; the only two occurrences in the whole repo are the pre-existing sentences in parity_claim and ccl.py's docstring that NAME the rule itself ('the steer forbids the phrase CUDA parity unqualified'), both unchanged by this pass
hard_rules_upheld.multi_device_peer_access_unchanged: MULTI_DEVICE class count stayed at exactly 1; MATH.nccl_collectives was filed under MATH instead of MULTI_DEVICE for the identical hardware-blocked reason, on purpose
hard_rules_upheld.no_fabricated_receipts: every performance_gap marked measured cites a receipt path that exists on disk in receipts/headless/ and was read before being cited; every unmeasured entry states a specific reason, not a template sentence
hard_rules_upheld.unverified_api_claims_flagged: several entries (MATH.thrust, MEMORY.mapped_memory, COMPILER.fatbinaries and others) explicitly mark a CUDA API behavior claim as reasoned from general knowledge rather than verified against NVIDIA documentation on this machine, per instruction

PROGRAMMING_MODEL: texture and surface memory / texture objects (cudaTextureObject_t) -- the read-only texture cache path, distinct from the __ldg-style read-only cache hint

the raw WMMA API (wmma::load_matrix_sync/mma_sync/store_matrix_sync) as its own capability, as distinct from cuBLAS/CUTLASS using tensor cores internally -- this census discussed tensor cores only through MATH.cublas_library_surface and MATH.cutlass_concepts, never the raw intrinsic
grid.sync() specifically, as a named sub-feature of EXECUTION.cooperative_groups -- the entry covers the group concept generally but not this one call in isolation
the CUDA driver API (cuCtxCreate/cuModuleLoad and friends) as distinct from the runtime API (cudaMalloc et al.) that every other entry in this ledger implicitly assumes
MEMORY: L2 cache persistence controls (cudaAccessPolicyWindow) for pinning hot data in L2 across kernel launches
ECC memory and its performance/capacity tradeoff -- not applicable to this machine's consumer silicon, but never explicitly ruled in or out the way MULTI_DEVICE.peer_access's hardware block was
texture/surface memory as a MEMORY concept (see PROGRAMMING_MODEL above -- listed once, not censused twice)
EXECUTION_STREAMS_AND_GRAPHS: CUDA Graphs conditional nodes (data-dependent branching inside an instantiated graph, a newer CUDA Graphs feature)

cudaEvent_t as a distinct capability from RUNTIME.streams_and_events' general treatment -- specifically inter-stream wait (cudaStreamWaitEvent) semantics and event-based timing (cudaEventElapsedTime), which PROFILING.kernel_timing touches only as 'the CUDA mechanism it is compared against', not as its own census line

CUDA driver-level context and Multi-Process Service (MPS) for sharing one GPU's SMs across processes with hardware partitioning -- distinct from ordinary multi-stream/multi-process time-slicing, and NOT to be confused with Apple's own 'MPS' (Metal Performance Shaders), a naming collision worth flagging so a future pass does not conflate the two
COMPILER: the CUDA driver's JIT cache (the on-disk PTX->SASS cache CUDA itself maintains across process runs) as distinct from COMPILER.jit_kernel_compilation's measurement of MLX's JIT, which is a different runtime's cache entirely
PTX ISA versioning and forward/backward compatibility rules

separate compilation and cross-object device linking as a build system question (distinct from COMPILER.link_time_optimization, which covers the OPTIMIZATION step, not the linking mechanics themselves)
MATH_ECOSYSTEM: cuBLASXt (multi-GPU BLAS) and cuBLASMg -- blocked on the same missing-hardware reason as MATH.nccl_collectives, not separately censused
cuDNN's specific convolution ALGORITHMS (Winograd, implicit GEMM, FFT-based) as opposed to MATH.cudnn_graph_engine_model's treatment of the engine-selection ARCHITECTURE only
AmgX / cuSPARSE's iterative-solver-specific pieces beyond the sparse-format/SpMM surface MATH.cusparse names
nvJPEG, nvCOMP, and other narrow single-purpose CUDA-X libraries outside the eleven named in the census brief
PROFILING: the compute-sanitizer initcheck and synccheck tools' SPECIFIC detection mechanisms in more depth than DEBUGGING.race_and_memory_diagnostics' single combined entry gives them
cuda-gdb's specific debugging feature set (breakpoints, single-stepping device code) as distinct from DEBUGGING.numerical_diagnostics' oracle-comparison practice
Nsight Graphics (as opposed to Nsight Systems/Compute) -- not relevant to a compute-only workload but never explicitly ruled out as such

not_yet_censused_reading: every item above is ABSENT FROM THE LEDGER, which under this campaign's own rule means NOT YET STUDIED, never NOT NEEDED. Several (WMMA intrinsics, MPS/MIG, conditional graph nodes) are plausibly HIGH relevance and were left out only because this pass's 48-entry scope was already large, not because they were judged unimportant.
